question: Source for building footprints in Montana, and the join of state address points to those shapes so one dot sits on each house.
bottom_line: Building shapes: use the FEMA and ORNL USA Structures file for Montana (MT_Structures_20260913.zip, 173,088,786 bytes, dated 2026-09-13): 918,052 structure footprints in a file geodatabase, WGS 84. Its own metadata states no access or use constraints, and the Esri-hosted copy of the same layer states CC BY 4.0, so FEMA should confirm the licence in writing before publishing. Do not use the Microsoft footprints (ODbL; 773,199 features in prior evidence) or Overture buildings (ODbL theme): publishing tiles derived from them would make the tiles a share-alike database under ODbL section 4.4. Join: the 674,715 Montana State Library address points join to footprints by location. In the Billings test box, 535 of 869 points sit inside a footprint, 313 are within 15 m of one, and 21 are farther; 131 of 307 footprints hold no address point inside. Simplifying to 0.5 m or 1 m saves almost nothing (-0.1% and -0.9% statewide), so skip that step.
recommendation: One source: the USA Structures Montana file dated 2026-09-13 (918,052 footprints), attributed to ORNL and FEMA. Ship 5-decimal [lon,lat] rings with no Douglas-Peucker pass. Footprint payload per tile (closing vertex and holes included): statewide median 427 bytes at zoom 15 (3 footprints) and 272 bytes at zoom 17 (2 footprints); p99 26,471 and 5,812 bytes; the densest zoom-15 tile in the Billings box is 57,036 bytes of JSON (10,773 bytes gzip) for 328 footprints, and the densest zoom-17 tile is 6,384 bytes (1,190 gzip) for 50 footprints. Address dots (coordinates plus street text, about 44 bytes per record): zoom-15 tile median 87 bytes and p99 11,550; zoom-17 median 43 and p99 2,143. Dot rule: one dot per footprint that holds at least one address point inside it or within 15 m, placed at a point inside the footprint, listing the deduplicated addresses; every address point farther than 15 m gets its own dot (12.1% statewide, 2.4% in Billings); footprints with no address are drawn as shape only (60.2% of statewide footprints hold no address point inside). Do not describe any shape as a damage or condition finding; the producer ran no formal accuracy test.

OUTBLDG and SEC_OCC are blank for all 918,052 features, and HEIGHT is filled for 3,552 (0.4%). A roof-height or outbuilding filter is not possible from this file.

Address records: 401 North 27th Street has three MSL records (two at one spot), so the dot rule must deduplicate. MSL live counts differ from the file (674,469 vs 674,715 statewide; 886 vs 869 in the Billings box); not reconciled.

Brief coordinate: 45.7836 N, 108.5047 W is inside the footprint of 175 North 27th Street and about 299 m from the 401 North 27th Street address point (45.785706 N, 108.507092 W). Check the brief's coordinate before using it as a fixture.

Microsoft count 773,199 is prior evidence and was not re-verified in this run (the stored copy the prior record names is not on disk). Overture Montana count was not obtained: 512 parquet files, 276.9 GB listed; a bounding-box read was not run (download and time budget).

Tile method: each footprint is assigned to the tile holding its centroid, with no clipping at tile edges. Per-tile totals exclude the outer array wrapper (2 bytes plus commas; 329 bytes in the densest zoom-15 Billings tile). Clipping at tile edges would add bytes; not measured.

Accuracy: the metadata ties positional accuracy to the imagery (WorldView under 3.5 m, NAIP at least 5 m). Simplification at 0.5 or 1 m and 5-decimal rounding (up to 0.67 m in the Billings box) are below that, so simplification buys almost nothing. Six-decimal rounding costs 8.9% more bytes in the Billings box for a 0.07 m rounding error.
The statewide Hausdorff figures are from a 20,000-feature random sample; the Billings figures are over every footprint in the box.

GDAL printed a performance warning that a polygon has more than 100 parts; the parsed geometry has at most 9 polygon parts per feature (915 features have more than one part). The warning source was not identified.
The Scientific Data descriptor says the national inventory has more than 125 million structures; the national count and the Montana share of it were not checked.
The Esri-hosted layer's address and occupancy fields may differ from the file (older edition); a single authoritative edition must be pinned in the build and in the About page.
legal_reading: ODbL (Microsoft Montana footprints; Overture buildings theme): if the site publishes tiles cut from these footprints, the tiles are a derived database. Section 4.4 a requires that a derived database the public uses be released under ODbL or a compatible licence, and section 4.4 b says that extracting a substantial part into a new database is a derived database. Section 4.6 then requires that the site also offer a machine-readable copy of the whole derived database, or the method of making it, at no more than reasonable cost. Section 4.3 requires a notice on rendered maps. In plain words: the joined address and footprint layer would have to be released under ODbL with its own machine-readable copy. That is a share-alike duty and is not recommended for a published site.

CC BY 4.0 (the USA Structures copy hosted by Esri, stated as CC BY 4.0): section 3(a)(1) requires credit to the creators (ORNL and FEMA), a copyright or licence notice, a link to the licence, and an indication that the data were changed. There is no share-alike duty. This is the cleanest licence for published tiles, provided FEMA confirms it for the 2026-09-13 file, whose own metadata says None.

Public domain: 17 U.S.C. 105 says copyright is not available for a work of the United States Government, and section 101 defines that as a work prepared by an officer or employee of the United States Government as part of official duties. ORNL staff are not shown here to be federal employees, so the public-domain route is not established by this definition alone. The Montana State Library address file states that its data are publicly available and non-sensitive and carries a use disclaimer, but it names no licence. The National Address Database inputs to PROP_ADDR are public domain per the prior record (data.gov catalog, not re-checked in this run).

Decision 7 (follow the laws): use the USA Structures file under its CC BY 4.0 statement, with an attribution line for ORNL and FEMA, a licence link, and a note that footprints are simplified or rounded and joined to addresses. Get FEMA's written licence for the 2026 file before the first publish. Do not publish tiles cut from the Microsoft footprints or from Overture (ODbL). Use the MSL address points with the MSL disclaimer and ask MSL to state a licence. Counsel should confirm the LightBox SmartParcels and HIFLD inputs to occupancy class before any OCC_CLS field is shown.
